name: Bika Ambon
description: A porous, honeycomb-textured cake from Medan made with tapioca, coconut milk, and pandan, springy and aromatic.
ingredients: a handful of fresh kaffir lime leaves, chopped
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with coconut oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the jasmine rice and ground cumin until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the lime wedges with the tamarind water until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 30 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
Garnish with cilantro or a dusting of crispy fried shallots.
tips: Bring your lime wedges to room temperature before mixing for a smoother, more even texture.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
For the cleanest slices, chill the finished dessert thoroughly before cutting.
